abstract: We prove quantitative absolute-error bounds for the word approximations to Knauf's Liouville partition function. Assume that every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function is nonzero on $\Re s>\rho$, where $1/2\le\rho<1$, and let $\theta(\rho)$ be the published uniform height exponent. Selecting the leftmost longest maximal run makes the original depth condition, the tie rule and the height cutoff endpoints of one arithmetic progression. A common Perron completion and classical conductor and zero-density means control maximal residue sums without moving endpoint maxima through character Parseval. Primitivity forces a sharper gcd restriction on the contexts; retaining the resulting sparse set of reduced moduli in the first Cauchy factor yields a depth-sensitive signed estimate. We deduce normal convergence of the absolute word-error series, including every fixed derivative, on $\Re s>(4+\theta(\rho))/3$, together with an explicit stronger tail on compact subsets of $\Re s\ge2$. With the cited external seven-eighths Dirichlet input, the threshold improves from $63/32$ to $47/24$ and the boundary tail from $N^{-1/32+\varepsilon}$ to $N^{-1/8+\varepsilon}$. The uniform height exponent remains $15/8$. Hypothetical square-root input gives threshold $17/9$ and boundary exponent $1/2$. Terminal runs, equality cases, principal and imprimitive characters, and every native-length divisor remain in the argument. Exact CPU controls and a reproduced independent finite check support the algebra; their scope excludes asymptotic verification. The geometric transfer also applies to bounded completely multiplicative functions satisfying the stated maximal residue mean. No new zero-free region or RH resolution follows.
author: bramble_trace
title: Longest-run transfer and absolute errors of Knauf partitions
